title: Reconstructing Cyano-bacteriophage P-SSP7 structure without imposing symmetry
protocol: Determine the icosahedral orientation of the particles using the MPSA procedure.
Store the alignment parameters in a separate list file in EMAN format.
Use a box size of 720 pixels (1.17 Å/pixel) for icosahedral reconstruction.
Include the tail protein apparatus at one of the 5-fold vertices for asymmetric reconstruction, corresponding to a box size of 960 pixels (1.17 Å/pixel).
Binarize the single particle images by a factor of 2 to a size of 480 pixels (2.34 Å/pixel) for Fourier synthesis.
Modify the particle centering parameters in the list file accordingly after binning.
Adjust center 120 pixels in both X and Y directions due to box size enlargement.
Shrink the adjusted center by 2 due to image resizing.
Reconstruct an initial 3D model using the EMAN _make3d_ program.
Lower the display threshold of the initial icosahedral reconstruction map from 2.54 to 0.12.
Visualize the "tail" at each of the 12 5-fold vertices as ghost densities.
Produce a tail mask in Amira software loosely fitting around the ghost density along the +Z-axis.
Add a positive constant of 0.5 to the 3D icosahedral density map using Chimera to make negative density visible.
Extract an initial tail model from the icosahedral model using the generated tail mask.
Low-pass filter the extracted tail model in EMAN using the _proc3d_ program.
Create a database of all possible tail mask projections.
Project the initial 3D tail mask along altitude angles from 0° to 90° at an interval of 3°.
Exclude azimuthal rotation as a projection parameter.
Project masks for different in-plane Euler angle orientations.
Index each mask by its projection orientation for computational efficiency.
Merge every three consecutive projections starting from the first projection at 0° to create looser masks, producing 11 projection masks from 0° to 90° at an interval of 9°.
Rotate each mask along the Z-axis with a step size of 0.5°, except for the 0° projection, generating in-plane rotation masks from 0° to 360°.
Merge every 20 rotations and index them to the angle corresponding to the middle (10th) mask, producing 36 in-plane rotation masks for each altitude angle.
Generate a total of 361 (1+10×36) 2D tail masks covering all possible asymmetric orientations of the particle.
Round the particle’s orientation to the nearest index orientation when picking a 2D tail mask during dynamic masking, ignoring the azimuthal orientation.
Distribute the process to 10 CPUs using EMAN’s _runpar_ program.
Simultaneously generate 40 random projections on each node.
Merge these 10 projection sets together into one.
Round each of the 60 equivalent icosahedral orientations to the nearest index orientation in the 2D tail mask database.
Extract the corresponding mask from the 2D tail mask database.
Apply the extracted mask to the particle image.
Compute cross common line correlations between each masked region and the 400 2D tail model reference projections.
Calculate residual values using the formula Σ_i (0.5 - cos(φ_i)).
Focus on a subset of frequency space between 1/200-1/60Å^-1 for calculating residuals during the first iteration.
Choose the orientation with the smallest residual as the particle's asymmetric orientation for the first iteration.
Process each of the 36,000 particles to determine their initial asymmetric orientations.
Reconstruct a 3D density map free of any symmetry using the EMAN _make3d_ program.
Use just the tail to generate masks and reference projections for the second iteration.
Starting from the third iteration, use both the tail and portal densities as the asymmetric target.
Repeat steps 2-7 with different resolution cut-offs: 45Å for the second iteration.
Continue refining with a 35Å resolution cut-off for the third iteration.
Proceed to refine using a 25Å resolution cut-off for the fourth iteration.
For the fifth iteration, use a 18Å resolution cut-off.
Extend the resolution cut-off to 12Å for the final couple of iterations.
Compare orientations determined at 12Å with those from the fifth iteration.
Retain only particles that were consistent from the fifth to the final iteration.
